messages:
ana: Heads-up — since ~09:10 UTC we're seeing intermittent packet loss between worker pools in us-west-2. Pods doing large model checkpoints or sharded allreduce fail briefly, jobs retry and queue up. Noticed mostly on GPU backfill nodes.

mike: Seen it too, noticed increased retransmits on grpc between trainer pods. Might be east-west only; north-south looks fine.

julia: Any pattern on which AZ or node types? RDMA-enabled or normal?

ana: (typo) meant ana — this looks concentrated in az-b and az-c, both use Mellanox cards on 5.18 kernel. Some pods in az-a are OK.

mike: I grabbed a quick tcpdump on pod-to-pod across two nodes:

```
# tcpdump -i eth0 host 10.32.5.12 and host 10.32.6.8
12:01:03.123456 IP 10.32.5.12.50000 > 10.32.6.8.50051: Flags [P.], seq 123:789, ack 456, win 65535
12:01:03.234567 IP 10.32.6.8.50051 > 10.32.5.12.50000: Flags [.], ack 789, win 65535
12:01:03.345678 IP 10.32.5.12 > 10.32.6.8: UDP, length 1400
12:01:03.345690 IP 10.32.5.12 > 10.32.6.8: UDP, length 1400
```

mike: Saw bursts of UDP/encap packets dropped — looks like fragmentation or offload weirdness.

julia: Can you paste ethtool -k and qdisc stats?

mike: Sure:

```
# ethtool -k eth0
Features for eth0:
rx-checksumming: on
tx-checksumming: on (keep-tx-checksumming: on)
scatter-gather: on
tcp-segmentation-offload: on
generic-segmentation-offload: on
large-receive-offload: on

# tc -s qdisc show dev eth0
qdisc mq root: 0 packets
qdisc ingress ffff: 12 packets, 0 dropped
```

ana: I also ran `ss -s` on one node — elevated retransmits and some forged RSTs during bursts.

chris: Could be Geneve encapsulation interacting poorly with LRO/GRO/TSO on the NIC. We've had kernels where GSO+encap caused odd reassembly.

julia: Do we have any recent kernel or firmware upgrades in az-b/c?

ana: Host images rolled kernel -> 5.18.14 two days ago for security backports. Firmware was same.

mike: Repro steps I used: run iperf3 from a GPU node in az-b to another in az-c with mtu 8900 and geneve overlay. Intermittent packet loss shows at higher parallel streams.

julia: Quick mitigation — can we disable offloads for a canary node and see if the loss disappears? Something like: `ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off` on a suspect node.

mike: Will try on one backfill node now. I'll also capture with `tcpdump -w /tmp/geneve-canary.pcap` on both ends.

sre-bot: scheduled: capture started on node gpu-backfill-12 (ID: i-0abcde) — TTL 2h.

mike: After disabling offloads: traffic seems stable in my iperf run, retransmits dropped to normal. So offload interaction is probable.

julia: Good find. But disabling offloads cluster-wide hurts throughput/cpu usage — for long-running training that could increase time and cost. Need a plan.

ana: Hypothesis: kernel 5.18 + mlx5 driver + Geneve encap triggers wrong segmentation leading to dropped fragments on RX path. Could be LRO/GRO bug.

chris: Options: 1) pin affected nodes to older kernel/fabric firmware (rollback), 2) keep offloads disabled until driver fix, 3) vendor bug with Mellanox — open case, 4) change overlay MTU to 1450 to avoid fragmentation (but breaks jumbo perf).

mike: I filed a quick bug with vendor with pcap + ethtool output. Case # MF-8421.

julia: Short-term mitigation: schedule a canary pool with offloads disabled and change kube-scheduler taints so new GPU jobs avoid affected nodes. We should also set autoscaler to prefer unaffected AZ (az-a) while investigation proceeds.

ana: I'll create a taint and cordon the ten worst nodes in az-b/c and add a runbook entry.

mike: I'll coordinate with infra-ops to roll a firmware/kernel rollback candidate on 2 test hosts tomorrow.

chris: Also recommend adding a synthetic job in CI that streams small UD/encap packets across AZs to detect regression earlier.

julia: Good call. Add metric: geneve_packet_drop_rate and alert at 0.5% over 5m.

sre-bot: alert created: geneve_packet_drop_rate (threshold: 0.5% / 5m) — alert ID A-9912.

ana: Action items:
- ana: cordon/taint affected nodes + runbook (ETA 1h)
- mike: collect full pcap, vendor case, test rollback (ETA 6h for initial rollback test)
- chris: define CI synthetic test and metric (ETA EOD)
- julia: adjust scheduler + create alert (done)

mike: One more thing — some of the failing pods do RDMA-based allreduce (ibverbs). If RDMA bypasses kernel and uses HCA, that path might be unaffected; it's more the TCP/UDP-over-geneve path causing issues. Keep that in mind for root cause.

ana: Noted. I'll prioritize GPU jobs with RDMA affinity to the healthier AZ while we triage.

julia: Thanks all. If anyone sees a sudden spike in job failures, @here ping this thread and we'll escalate. :eyes:
